About Event

📅 Saturday, October 24, 2026 | 1:00PM - 9:00PM
📍 UC San Diego | Student Services Center MPR
🍕 Dinner, drinks, and snacks provided
c0mpiled , by Transpose Platform , is excited to host c0mpiled-16: UC San Diego , featuring Latted (YC W24) & Gutgutgoose (YC S26) 🚀
Builders will compete for cash prizes, collaborate with talented students, and connect with YC alumni judges.
Join us for an evening of building, meeting driven founders, and turning bold ideas into real products.
Challenge: Invisible Interfaces
The best interface is sometimes no interface at all. This edition explores products that work through voice, motion, sensors, live data, autonomous agents, and other natural interactions.
Build technology that helps people or systems sense, decide, and act without relying on a traditional app or screen.
1. Dispatch
Use live data such as ship traffic, flight data, fleet GPS, sensors, or border wait times to move physical things where they need to go.
Build for logistics, transportation, ports, emergency response, or defense.
2. No App
Build for people who will never open an app, including seniors, drivers, nurses, warehouse workers, and field crews.
Use voice, phone calls, glasses, vibration, or another invisible interface. If users have to look at a screen, it does not count.
3. Unsupervised
Build agents that run for hours without constant supervision.
Your system should know when it is stuck, overspending, looping, or when it needs to stop.
4. AI-Powered Consumer Products for 1 Billion People
Build an AI-powered consumer product that reaches people through natural, ambient, or invisible interactions.
Rethink how people discover, use, and benefit from technology beyond traditional apps and screens. The strongest ideas will address a clear everyday need and have the potential to serve people at global scale.
Prizes
🥇 1st Place: $2,000 | 🥈 2nd Place: $1,200 | 🥉 3rd Place: $800
Judges - All are hiring for Full-time/Internships
Metehan Oz — Latted (YC W24)

Anis Mihrshahi Gutgutgoose (YC S26) [Remote]

Leon Mojarrabi Gutgutgoose (YC S26) [Remote]

Neel Majmudar — Transpose Platform

Anamika Khaleghian - Corgi (YC S24)

Sankeerth Rao Karingula, Ph.D. - Agentin AI (YC W25)

Punn Kam - Conduit (YC W24)

Pavan Kumar - Clean (YC F26)

Christa Lilien Tsao - Meadow (EF S26)

Arjun Vad - Agencity

Schedule
1:00PM: Check-in and networking

1:45PM: Challenge overview

2:00PM: Building begins

7:30PM: Submissions due and optional demos

8:30PM - 9:00PM: Awards and closing

Feel free to group up or go solo. You can have 1-4 people per team . If you are part of a group, every group member must sign up separately through Luma.
Whether you are new to vibecoding or an experienced builder, this is a space to prototype quickly, learn from people who have built before, and showcase your talent.
You must be registered on Luma to attend the event.
Spots are limited. Come ready to build!

About Event

Night Hack is back at Founders, Inc. on October 30.
Come make something you want to show off. A robot. An agent. A game. That side project you can't stop thinking about.
You'll have five hours to build. Then show us what works.
Last time: nearly 1,000 signups and 120+ projects submitted in five hours.
The night:
4:15pm: Check-in + team formation

5–10pm: Build

10pm: Exhibition + judging
followed by finalist demos & awards

11pm: Close

No re-entry after 10pm.
Prizes + builder perks
Cash prizes, tools to build with, and $10,000 in Anthropic API prize credits up for grabs .
Anthropic is also providing $50 in API credits per builder.
We’re finalizing the cash-prizes & additional perks. Award details and redemption instructions will be shared ahead of the event.
Our partners
Firecrawl helps AI applications search, crawl and extract useful data from the web.
Bolt helps you build apps and websites by chatting with AI.
Convex brings your app’s backend together with a realtime database and server functions.
Anthropic , the team behind Claude, is returning with API credits for builders and prize credits for the top three teams.
What to build
Start something new or add a substantial capability to an existing project. Existing code, models and hardware are welcome. Judges evaluate the work completed during the sprint.
Live demos. No slides.
Come solo or in teams of up to four. Every teammate must apply individually and receive approval.
Bringing hardware?
Bring your complete setup, tools, cables, chargers and a software or simulation fallback. Hardware requires advance review for space, power and safety.
We cannot provide hardware or electronics-lab access, including soldering, fabrication and 3D printing. Bringing your own printer requires approval.
Everyone should bring a laptop and charger.
Approved builders receive Discord access and final instructions after confirming through Luma. Photography and recording may take place. Builders under 18 need parent or guardian permission.

Registration

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Register

About Event

Please find the hackathon website here . That includes all the rules and resources.
Join us for the Patch the Conference Hackathon, right before GitHub Universe, where we're looking for builders who can find what's broken about conferences and ship the patch. If something about conferences has ever bugged you, from finding the right people to meet to working out which talk is actually worth your time, this is your chance to build the fix.
Everyone building gets free OpenAI credits and $50 in Bright Data credits, plus plenty of swag. Pick a track, build something that works, and show it off on stage at the end of the day.
Age Requirement: This event is 21+. Valid government-issued photo ID will be checked at the door, no exceptions. Please come prepared with your ID, as entry will not be granted without one.
🏆 Prizes
Best use of FalkorDB: iPhone Duos

Best use of Bright Data: $1,500

Best use of TrueForge with OpenAI: $1,000

Best use of Qodo: $500

If you win and don't want the phone, you can take the cash prize instead.
🗓️ Agenda
9:00 AM: Doors open

9:00 AM to 10:00 AM: Grab breakfast, get set up, start hacking and get familiar with the tools

10:00 AM to 11:00 AM: Workshops and talks from our sponsors to get you up and running

11:00 AM to 2:00 PM: Back to building

2:00 PM: Pizzas arrive, lunch is served

2:00 PM to 5:30 PM: Keep hacking and submit your project

5:30 PM to 6:30 PM: Presentations and judging, with teams showcasing their projects on stage

6:30 PM: Winners announced and the iPhone Duos handed over

7:00 PM: Event wraps up

🎁 Credits for everyone
OpenAI: free credits so you can use OpenAI models in your project at no cost.

Bright Data: $50 in credits to pull live data from the web.

Details on how to claim them will be shared at the event.
🛠️ Tracks
Track 1: FalkorDB (iPhone Duos)
FalkorDB is an open-source graph database built for AI agents. Agents are only as good as the context they work with, and a graph gives yours connected data it can reason over, a memory it keeps between sessions, and a clear picture of how things relate. It runs locally with Docker, you query it with Cypher, and it works with Python, Node.js, Java, Rust, Go, PHP and C#.
How to use it:
Follow connections across data: let your agent answer questions that take more than one hop, with graph queries as its tools.

Remember across sessions: store conversation history and what the agent has learned, so it picks up where it left off.

Share state between agents: give multiple agents one graph to read and write, so handoffs between them work.

Connect people, projects and decisions: bring knowledge from docs, tickets and chats into one graph.

Show the path behind an answer: trace every answer back to the data it came from.

Ideas to get you started:
A conference concierge that answers "which talks on agents are on after lunch, and who's speaking?" and shows the path through the graph behind its answer.

A networking agent that suggests who to meet based on shared topics and projects, and remembers who you've already spoken to.

A schedule planner where several agents share one graph to plan your day, sort out clashes and send follow-ups after the event.

Judging criteria:
Graph at the core: FalkorDB does real work, like multi-hop queries, memory or shared state between agents, not just storing rows.

Explainable answers: you can show how the project got to its answer through the graph.

Solves a real conference problem: something attendees, speakers or organisers would actually use.

Working demo: it runs live on stage.

Track 2: Bright Data ($1,500)
Conference week runs on live web data: hotel and flight prices that change hourly, side events scattered across sites, attendee info spread across dozens of pages. The hardest of these sites block scripts, so what works once fails at scale.

Bright Data gives your app or agent reliable access to that public data and returns clean, structured results, with blocks, CAPTCHAs, JavaScript rendering and parsing handled for you.
How to use it:
Web Scraper APIs: ready-made scrapers that return structured JSON from sites like Booking, Tripadvisor, Trip.com and Airbnb. No need to build a scraper when you have a ready made template, this is the quickest way to get real data.

Scraper Studio: build a custom scraper for any site without one, with self-healing when layouts change.

Web Unlocker API: fetch pages from sites that usually block bots.

Browser API: run Playwright or Puppeteer on a remote browser for JavaScript-heavy sites.

Bright Data MCP and SERP API: let your agent search the web and read any page as clean markdown, or get structured results from Google and Bing.

Your $50 in credits covers trying any of these.
Ideas to get you started:
A stay finder that compares hotel prices near the venue, tracks flights, and tells you when to book.

A side event radar that pulls events, happy hours and parties around the conference into one feed.

A who-to-meet scout that uses LinkedIn profiles and company data to rank the people worth finding.

A "should I go?" agent that checks a conference's past talks, recordings and reviews before you buy a ticket.

Judging criteria:
Hard-to-get data at the core: the project depends on Bright Data for fresh data from sites a basic script can't reliably reach.

Data quality: the data is accurate, up to date and handled well when a site changes or a request fails.

Usefulness: it saves people real time or money around conferences.

Working demo: it runs live on stage.

Track 3: TrueForge with OpenAI ($1,000)
Build an agent on TrueForge, powered by OpenAI models using your free credits.
TrueForge is TrueFoundry's open-source agent harness, the runtime that turns a model into a working agent. It handles the agent loop for you: calling the model, connecting MCP tools, spinning up a sandbox only when the agent needs to run code, loading skills, and pausing for human approval when you want it to. It comes with a chat UI and a TypeScript SDK, and you can run it locally with one command: npx @truefoundry/trueforge
How to use it:
Run TrueForge locally and connect an OpenAI model with your credits.

Give your agent tools by connecting MCP servers, so it can act on real data and services.

Use the sandbox for anything that needs code to run, skills for repeatable instructions, and approvals before the agent does anything you'd want to check first.

Build your own interface with the SDK, or use the chat UI that comes with it.

Ideas to get you started:
A speaker agent that helps you find open CFPs, draft a talk proposal and track deadlines, and asks before submitting anything.

A follow-up agent that turns the contacts and notes from your day into personalised follow-up emails, and waits for your approval before sending.

A session feedback agent that runs code in the sandbox to analyse attendee feedback and turn it into a clear report for organisers.

Working demo: it runs live on stage.

Request to Join

About Event

In this 10+ hour intensive hackathon led by the research team at Obvious you will build your autonomous software factory. TLDR: you'll be able to start assigning your agents features to build instead of prompts.
Note: This event is entirely free, including unlimited tokens for the hackathon. Building and tokens will be using an obvious.ai workspace.
We will be awarding over $30K in token prizes to the teams that can build the most in a day!
1st place receives $20,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

2nd place receives $10,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

3rd place receives $5,000 worth of Obvious Fusion credits

Come alone or come as a team. If you want to valuemaxx this event (and set yourself up to win big) the ideal group to bring is:
a technical founder or engineering leader

a product manager (if you have one)

1+ engineers (the more ai-pilled the better)

What to bring
Your laptop

Access to a real Github repo you care about [or] a clear vision for a greenfield project

A bug backlog or a list of small improvements

We'll set up your Obvious workspace and go through onboarding in-person. Meals and drinks are provided.
Agenda
10:00 AM – Doors Open
10:30 AM – Opening Session
11:00 AM – Building Begins
12:45 PM – Lunch, with Lightning Talks
3:30 PM – Optional Q&A with Obvious
5:15 PM – Closing Panel
5:45 PM – Awards & Happy Hour
What you’ll be learning:
How to...
design the complete hands-off build loop

manage a multi-pr autonomous agent swarm

prepare more ambitious builds (entire features or even products)

manage QA, code review, and human feedback without slowing down the work

decide where to spend time vs go hands off

rethink both devops and organizational roles in a world of autonomy

scale autonomous software delivery safely

think about roadmap and software design when you can build anything practical in a day

This is for the Engineer & Technical Builder track of our hackathon. If you're interested in learning more about the Product Manager track, check out and register at this Luma: https://luma.com/frontier-builders
What building on the Frontier is like:

-------
About Obvious:
Obvious is an applied AI research lab with a focus on autonomous product development. We spend our days closing the gap between what's possible and what's doable, treating our own company as the experiment for what it means to operate at agent scale. We've reinvented our product, reshaped our team, accelerated revenue, and 10x'd our shipping velocity in less than a year. At peak velocity we've shipped 1000 PRs in one day with 10 engineers.
Frontier is where we do our best to hand that system to other teams. We're excited to work with you!
→ Learn more at obvious.ai/events

About Event

Build physical AI applications with real robot arms.

About the Event
Viam and MongoDB are excited to host a two-day, hands-on hackathon for curious, ambitious builders who want to go deep on physical AI. You'll get a real robot arm and support from Viam experts throughout.
No prior robotics experience is required, just an interest in physical AI and some software experience.
Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis.

What You'll Build
Working in a team of 2-3, you'll build an end-to-end robotics application using Viam and a real robot arm.

Each team will have access to:
UFactory xArm or Universal Robots arm with a two-finger gripper attachment (feel free to also bring your own SO-101)

Linux compute machine

RealSense D435 or Orbbec Astra 2 camera (fixed to arm)

Webcams

A free Viam account

A MongoDB Atlas cluster for storing and querying your robot's data: sensor readings, grasp attempts, run logs and embeddings

We’ll provide a variety of objects for your robot to manipulate. You are encouraged to bring anything required for the project you have in mind.
Please bring your own laptop.
In your application, please summarize what project you have in mind.
Ideas from past events: training a VLA, playing chess, mixing a cocktail, quality inspection, drawing a picture, puzzle insertion, manipulating a robot arm using computer vision and hand gestures.
Build with MongoDB Atlas
Robots produce a lot of data, and the best teams use it.
Every team gets MongoDB Atlas to give their robot a memory. Some ideas:
Log every attempt (poses, gripper force, camera metadata, success or failure) and query it to tune your approach between runs

Use Atlas Vector Search to match what the camera sees against known objects, which helps with the recycling sort or open-track ideas

Store task plans, scene descriptions or past outcomes so an LLM-driven robot can retrieve context before it acts

Build a live dashboard of your benchmark runs

Using Atlas isn't required, but strong, creative uses of it will stand out to the judges.
Prizes
We'll award prizes to a total of three teams. Each member of a winning team will take home SO-101 pre-assembled robot kits, including: a leader arm, a follower arm, and a camera + Viam credits.
Gold: SO-101 arm + $5,000 in MongoDB Atlas credits and $5,000 in Viam credits

Silver: SO-101 arm + $2,500 in MongoDB Atlas credits and $2,500 in Viam credits

Bronze: SO-101 arm + $1,000 in MongoDB Atlas credits and $1,000 in Viam credits

Please bring your own laptop. We recommend taking our free online course Viam 101 (est time: 45-90mins) ahead of time. Even if you only go through the first lessons, it will help you get the hang of things quickly.
Schedule
Thursday, October 29
9:00 AM: Check-in and breakfast
9:30 AM: Kickoff: Welcome & crash course on building with Viam and MongoDB
10:00 AM: Teams and hardware
10:30 AM: Hacking begins
1:00 PM: Lunch
6:00 PM: Dinner
9:00 PM: Hard close: Robots power down, doors close (no overnight hacking)
Friday, October 30
9:00 AM: Doors open, breakfast
9:30 AM: Hacking resumes
12:30 PM: Lunch
3:30 PM: Demos and drinks
5:00 PM: Awards
6:00 PM: Event concludes
What Skills You Need
No robotics experience required, but you should be comfortable with:
Coding: Python, Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, or C++

Linux: Using SSH and running basic terminal commands

JSON: Reading and editing configuration files

Git: Basic workflows so your team can build together

Bonus: knowing how to plug in a pre-trained vision model (like YOLO or OpenCV) to help the robot see and identify objects (not required)

Bonus: Some familiarity with MongoDB or document databases (not required, and mentors can help you get started)

Before the Event
We recommend taking our free online course Viam 101 (est time: 45-90mins) ahead of time. Even the first few lessons will help you get the hang of things quickly. You may optionally take MongoDB x Viam Hackathon Learning Path to get oriented with MongoDB Atlas, even completing the first few lessons can help you hit the ground running.

Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis.
We’ll select a curated group of ambitious software developers and send official confirmations to accepted participants. Attendees must be approved in advance to participate.

We’re hosting the Party Games Track, looking for the next big living-room hit! Think multiplayer party games designed for the big screen, ideally for 2–6 players, where everyone joins by scanning a QR code on the TV and uses their phone as a controller.
We want games that make the room come alive! Think shouting, laughing, moving around, friendly competition, and unforgettable moments. The kind of gameplay that’s so entertaining people can’t resist pulling out their phones to share it on Instagram Stories, Snapchat, or TikTok.
The winning team will be invited to pitch their game to Weekend’s product and engineering teams and get feedback from the people behind our growing portfolio of TV games!
Random Games Track:
Anything goes. Platformers, puzzlers, roguelikes, narrative experiments, cozy sims, or something nobody has a genre name for yet. If it’s fun, surprising, and fits the theme, it belongs here.

Rosebud AI: Rosebud AI Game Maker helps people turn ideas into playable games. Describe what you imagine, build it in your browser, and share it with others.

Request to Join

About Event

🚀Make an impact on real world problems in a single weekend!🚀
HSI is back for our third year in a row! Join Hack for Social Impact once again to tackle real-world challenges . We are teaming up with non-profit partners to present you with important and well-scoped challenges, in partnership with UN Convention to Combat Desertification and 4 local nonprofits.
This event is supported by our sponsors: Gemini, Bild.ai , and Wefunder. Developers will receive credits during the hackathon to work on your projects from our sponsors and technology partners.
$5000 cash prizes in total for the winners of projects
This year, we've teamed up with incredible partners to tackle pressing issues in mental health, climate, justice reform, and art & design:

🌎 Climate : Work with the UN to build an interactive game to enable the community to participate in land planning! Block by Block is a Minecraft-based tool for communities to design their own streets, and has run in 55 countries since 2012. However, it is unsuited to UNCCD's work in real-world land planning: Minecraft has endless resources, arbitrary terrain, and no consequence to player actions. Build a game from real satellite and GIS data showing the impact of land use, to engage the community.
🌱 Community Resilience: The East Bay Permaculture Guild brings neighbors together through garden work parties, community gatherings, and local regeneration projects. But welcoming newcomers and promoting events across websites, email lists, and messaging groups falls on a handful of volunteers. Interest fades without follow-up, and repetitive outreach leaves organizers stretched thin. Build simple tools to help the Guild welcome new members, understand how they want to participate, and turn event details into outreach ready for volunteer review. Keep it affordable, easy for volunteers to maintain, and true to the personal connections that make the community worth joining.
🩷 Mental Health : Boundless Freedom Project can reach people inside with mindfulness and mental health practice through in-person sessions and the Edovo tablets. On release that support falls away, during the 30 days that hit hardest. Build something that keeps familiar practice at hand, holds as little personal information as possible, and assumes no smartphone and no dependable internet.
⚖️ Justice Reform : California's corrections department spends under one percent of its budget on rehabilitation. Transformative Programming Works advocates for them across 120 organizations, but so far can only track process data such as who enrolled and how long a class ran. Join disjoint records such as parole and recidivism data into a framework TPW, and nonprofits generally, can use to track impact.

🎨 Art & Design : BRIDGEGOOD's Oakland studio teaches designers to build with their own communities in mind, through conversations about identity, money and conflict that only work in a small room with a facilitator in it. That room seats a few dozen people a year. Find a way the practice can travel to designers who will never sit in it, without thinning into a slide deck.
🏆 Past winners went to present at UN Climate Conference and build startups that get accepted to YC and raise seed funding!🎯 Will your weekend hack be next year's success story?
✨Register your interest and follow us on our LinkedIn for more Partner & Prize announcements ✨
For more information on the event and a recap of last year, visit our website !
✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨

Whether you are a technical engineer or a non-technical innovator, if you want to team up with smart, driven people to create positive change, you belong here. Bring your unique skills and the energy to make the world a better place to spend the weekend solving real problems together.

About Event

One Day to Build Personal Agents
Saturday, Oct. 24th | Application Required
Join us in San Francisco for a focused, in-person hackathon to build personal agents.
We’re bringing together up to 50 ambitious engineers, including the incoming Puentes fellows ( https://x.com/GadiBorovich/status/2109684917886238817 ), to spend a day building personal agents that make life in San Francisco better. Expect live demos, prizes, food, coffee, and a room full of builders at First Round Capital’s office.
Capacity is limited; applications are required.
Who Should Apply
This is for you if you've shipped agents, tools, or you can show relevant repos and side projects. This hackathon is a way for you to meet other ambitious engineers in San Francisco.
What to Expect
Doors open at 9 am Saturday.

Kickoff talks start at 9:30 with team formation taking place immediately after.

We will have a focused 10-hour build sprint fueled by food and coffee.

Building ends at 6:30pm, followed immediately by demos.

Theme: Personal Agents for San Francisco
San Francisco is where people come to build the future. It’s also a city where plenty of everyday things could work better.
AI can start handling more of those things. Not just answering questions, but actually handling things: the calls, the forms, the scheduling, the follow-ups.
What would you want a personal agent to handle for you or someone else in San Francisco?
Whether you arrived last week or have lived here for years, pay attention. What surprised you? What’s harder than it should be? What works better somewhere else? What do you love about the city that more people should get to enjoy?
Software is unlimited. Let’s have fun with that and build something really useful.
Some places to start:
Retail and local businesses. Can an agent find something you need at a neighborhood shop, confirm it’s available, and arrange pickup? What would a shop owner want an agent handling every day?

Getting around. Can an agent coordinate your commute, errands, and appointments and figure out a new plan when something changes?

Hospitality. What could an agent take care of for a visitor, a host, or someone running a restaurant? Think reservations, requests, coordination, and all the back-and-forth.

Moving here. Can an agent help someone get settled, organize immigration paperwork, keep track of appointments, or navigate unfamiliar services?

These are starting points. Bring something you’ve noticed yourself.
We’re excited about projects that work, that we can demo, and that someone would want to keep using after the hackathon.

We’re bringing together up to 50 ambitious engineers, including the incoming Puentes fellows (https://x.com/GadiBorovich/status/2109684917886238817), to spend a day building personal agents that make life in San Francisco better. Expect live demos, prizes, food, coffee, and a room full of builders at First Round Capital’s office.
Capacity is limited; applications are required.
Who Should Apply
This is for you if you've shipped agents, tools, or you can show relevant repos and side projects. This hackathon is a way for you to meet other ambitious engineers in San Francisco.

What to Expect
Doors open at 9 am Saturday.
Kickoff talks start at 9:30 with team formation taking place immediately after.
We will have a focused 10-hour build sprint fueled by food and coffee.
Building ends at 6:30pm, followed immediately by demos.
Theme: Personal Agents for San Francisco
San Francisco is where people come to build the future. It’s also a city where plenty of everyday things could work better.
AI can start handling more of those things. Not just answering questions, but actually handling things: the calls, the forms, the scheduling, the follow-ups.
What would you want a personal agent to handle for you or someone else in San Francisco?
Whether you arrived last week or have lived here for years, pay attention. What surprised you? What’s harder than it should be? What works better somewhere else? What do you love about the city that more people should get to enjoy?
Software is unlimited. Let’s have fun with that and build something really useful.
Some places to start:
Retail and local businesses. Can an agent find something you need at a neighborhood shop, confirm it’s available, and arrange pickup? What would a shop owner want an agent handling every day?
Getting around. Can an agent coordinate your commute, errands, and appointments and figure out a new plan when something changes?
Hospitality. What could an agent take care of for a visitor, a host, or someone running a restaurant? Think reservations, requests, coordination, and all the back-and-forth.
Moving here. Can an agent help someone get settled, organize immigration paperwork, keep track of appointments, or navigate unfamiliar services?
These are starting points. Bring something you’ve noticed yourself.
We’re excited about projects that work, that we can demo, and that someone would want to keep using after the hackathon.

Ali Haghani — Co-founder, Circleback
Ray Fitzgerald — Founder & CEO, Bloom
Nicolás Montone — Software Engineer, Vercel

Felipe Pontiggia — Software Engineer, Circleback
Andrés Viera — Software Engineer, Circleback
Arthur Guiot — Software Engineer, Circleback
Prizes
Cash is king in this economy:
First: $1,000 USD
Second: $500 USD
Third: $250 USD
Rules & Submission Criteria
Projects will be submitted through DevPost’s portal.
Hosts
Antigravity Capital: early stage VC firm in San Francisco. We created Puentes to bridge the best talent in Latin America to Silicon Valley. Learn more: https://puentes.antigravity.capital.
Sponsors
TO BE ANNOUNCED
Selection & Format
Application-based: we review on a rolling basis.
Teams of up to 4 are welcome; solo builders can form teams on site.
In-person demoing is mandatory for all accepted participants.
Logistics
Bring your laptop and charger. Hosting it at First Round Capital's office.
Why This Weekend Exists
Puentes brings exceptional builders from Latin America to San Francisco. This hackathon brings them together with engineers already building here. https://puentes.antigravity.capital/.

About Event

HOW DO PRODUCTS ACTUALLY GROW?
Building products has never been easier. Getting real users, distribution, and revenue is still hard.
Local Align #3 — AI × GTM Day is a hands-on day for people who want to learn how products actually grow using AI-native GTM — from SEO/GEO and organic content to developer growth, community, outbound, automation, UGC, and distribution.
🎤 Learn from real growth stories.
Hear founders and operators break down how they went from 0 → 1,000+ users , built communities of 10,000+ , and generated millions of organic impressions without relying on paid acquisition. Pasted markdown
⚡ Put it into practice.
Choose from 6 real products with 6 real GTM problems and use AI, code, content, outbound, communities, automation, or whatever works to move real metrics: users, leads, signups, traffic, engagement, and conversions. Pasted markdown
🏆 6 Challenges · Max 2 Teams per Challenge
1 winning team per track · $200 cash per track · +$200 Grand Prize
When a challenge fills with 2 teams, 1 of those 2 teams wins the track prize.
☕ Come for the people too.
Not hacking? Come for the talks, startup demos, Coffee Chats, food, social, final pitches, and an afternoon with founders, engineers, creators, investors, students, and GTM operators from across the Bay Area.
Come to learn. Come to build. Come to meet your next collaborator, customer, cofounder — or simply someone worth knowing.
You do not need to compete to attend.
🎤 Learn: How Products Actually Grow
No generic startup advice.
Hear real 0→1 growth stories from founders and operators who have built audiences, acquired users, and turned distribution into a system.
Lucy Ye — Co-founder & COO, JobWizard.ai
SEO/GEO × Organic Content × AI-Native Growth
Built a 0→1 SEO engine that generated 2M+ Google Search impressions in 2 months , plus 1M+ organic video impressions with zero paid acquisition .
Learn how an early-stage startup turns search, content, and AI automation into repeatable distribution. Pasted markdown
Weijia — Founder & CEO, LingCode
Developer Growth × Product-Led Growth × Community
Built content reaching millions, grew a coding education platform from 0 → 10,000+ students , and took LingCode from launch to 1,000+ users in its first month .
Learn how technical founders can turn product, content, and community into an organic growth engine. Pasted markdown
Ben Weinmann — Growth @ Magnific
UGC × AI Content × Organic Growth × Attribution
Growth operator focused on organic distribution, UGC programs, AI-powered content, and short-form growth.
His experience spans OpenArt AI, Cluely, Magnific, and his own creator work, where his content and UGC programs have collectively generated 70M+ views .
Talk: From Views to Conversion: What Actually Works in UGC & AI Content Pasted markdown
More founders & GTM operators to be announced.
⚖️ Jury
The final challenge winners will pitch in front of a small jury of investors, founders, and operators.
Paula Ramoneda
VC & Corporate Innovation @ Plug and Play
additional startup / GTM judges

Each Challenge Owner selects the winner of their own track.
The jury then reviews the 6 track-winning teams and votes for 1 Overall Grand Prize winner .
No complicated scoring system.
Build → Grow → Show Proof → Pitch → Vote

⚡ Build: 6 Real Products. 6 Real Growth Problems.
Most hackathons ask you to build another demo.
Here, you'll work on a real product with real users and a real GTM problem — then use AI, code, content, outbound, SEO/GEO, automation, communities, partnerships, creators, or whatever else you can invent to move the numbers. Pasted markdown
💻 AI Developer Tools — LingCode
How do you win developers when every week brings another AI coding tool?
Grow an AI-native IDE through developer communities, technical content, product-led loops, GEO, creators, or your own growth automation.
Learn: developer GTM, PLG, community growth, and how technical products earn adoption. Pasted markdown
🎾 Consumer Community — Tennistry
3,500+ users. 1,500+ real tennis matches. How do you create the next 1,000?
Tennistry connects tennis players in real life.
Test local acquisition, referrals, ambassadors, events, creators, and ways to prove which users you actually brought in.
Learn: consumer growth, network effects, referral loops, local/community GTM, and attribution. Pasted markdown
🇺🇸 High-Trust Services — TurboNIW
How do you acquire customers when the decision is expensive, complex, and built on trust?
TurboNIW helps STEM researchers and professionals prepare for the EB-2 NIW process through structured educational materials and guidance.
Unlike a casual app download, customers may spend $1,000+ and are making a high-stakes career decision — making trust and intent central to acquisition.
Learn: high-intent SEO/GEO, trust-based funnels, educational content, lead qualification, and customer acquisition for high-consideration services. Pasted markdown
💳 Consumer FinTech — MaxWorth
30,000 users already. What becomes the next scalable growth channel?
MaxWorth is a North American credit-card management app entering its next stage of growth.
Explore finance content, SEO/GEO, creators, referrals, communities, partnerships, or new product-led acquisition loops.
Learn: consumer FinTech GTM, lifecycle growth, referral mechanics, content distribution, and scaling beyond early adopters. Pasted markdown
🎬 Generative AI × Entertainment — SceneMixer.com
A new AI creative product is starting from zero. Where do the first 100 real users come from?
SceneMixer is an AI short-drama generation platform.
Find the creators and communities most likely to care, then experiment with UGC, viral formats, creator seeding, social distribution, and product-led sharing.
Learn: 0→1 launches, creator GTM, UGC, viral loops, and consumer AI distribution. Pasted markdown
💹 Financial AI — Winus
How do you grow a financial AI product when trust, accuracy, and professional credibility matter as much as product experience?
Winus is a financial AI platform built for research and decision-making, combining financial chat, deep research, fact-checking, agents, and skills for finance professionals.
Test finance communities, professional content, SEO/GEO, partnerships, referrals, and other measurable GTM experiments.
Learn: financial AI GTM, trust-driven acquisition, professional-user growth, content distribution, and conversion in high-intent markets. Pasted markdown

About Event

Build it with OpenAI. Validate with Kane.
Kane CLI Hack Day SF, Supported by OpenAI.
Build it with an agent. Verify it with Kane.
Your agent can write an app in minutes. On October 24 you find out if that app actually works.
We're taking over a room in San Francisco for a full day of building with AI coding agents, with support from OpenAI. Kane CLI runs on OpenAI models under the hood, so for one Saturday the models that help write your code are also the ones checking it.
$30,000+ in prizes and credits
Saturday, October 24 · San Francisco · Hosted by TestMu AI, supported by OpenAI.
Seats are limited and every registration is reviewed. Apply early.
The Challenge
Build a working app with any AI coding agent. Use Kane CLI to prove it works. Ship by 6 PM.
That's all there is to it. Build a tool, a dashboard, a game, an internal utility, a strange experiment, or the side project that's been sitting in your notes app since spring. Just follow two rules:
Kane CLI has to verify your app. At minimum, run it at demo time. The teams that win will go further and put Kane inside the agent: a hook that runs Kane on every save, an agent that reads Kane's NDJSON output and keeps fixing until the flows pass, or a spec that compiles straight into Kane flows.

Your app has to run, ship and survive a live demo. Judges want to see it working in front of them.

Request to Join

About Event

🛑 Learning was never text-only. Kids read out loud, scribble on worksheets, point at diagrams, and think with their hands. Now AI can hear, see, and watch too.
SVAI Arrival Guide .pdf
Multi-Modal AI for Education
A text box only catches what a student types. A great teacher notices much more: the pause before a hard word, the crossed-out step in a math problem, the moment a class goes quiet. Multi-modal AI can finally pick up those signals. Voice, handwriting, images, and video can all become part of how we teach.
The hard part isn't the demo. It's building tools that teachers and families actually trust, and showing that students really learned more. That takes clear learning outcomes, not just a clever model.
Join Beta Fund and co-host Epic at Snowflake's Silicon Valley AI Hub in Menlo Park for a full day of building multi-modal learning tools. The day includes a panel with voices from Epic , Khan Academy , and Dex on where AI education is headed, plus demos in front of the room.
Build tutors that listen. Build tools that see the work. Build learning you can measure.
⚠️ Approval required. About 120 builders. You need an approved registration to get in: no walk-ins, no +1s. Bring your laptop.
🛠️ Join our Discord for credits, team formation, and support: Join Discord Server · 2-4 builders per team
Format
One-day, build-first hackathon in Menlo Park

2-4 builders per team

Every project uses at least two modalities: text plus voice/audio, images/handwriting, or video

Working demo required (3-minute demos)

Use public, synthetic, or consented data only. No real student records.

Hosts & Co-host
💡 Beta Fund ｜Silicon Valley fund backing AI founders from inception to seed. Invests $200K–$3M and is built on the Beta community of 500+ startups and 300,000+ founders.
💡 Beta University ｜Runs an 8-week pre-acceleration program that helps early-stage founders build VC-ready companies with proven know-how from Silicon Valley. Apply now!
📚 Epic ｜Co-host. The leading digital library for kids 12 and under, with 40,000+ books, audiobooks, and learning videos from 250+ publishers, used by teachers and families. Epic also co-hosted our AI + Education Hackathon at Stanford in September.
Venue Sponsor
📍 Snowflake Silicon Valley AI Hub ｜Our venue for the day, Snowflake's AI hub in Menlo Park. Thank you to Snowflake for hosting us.
📅 Agenda
9:00 AM Check-in & Breakfast
10:00 – 10:20 AM Opening remarks and kickoff
10:20 – 11:00 AM 🎤 Panel: What Multi-Modal AI Changes in Learning, with speakers from Epic, Khan Academy, and Dex
Panelists include Julia Horowitz, Head of Content at Epic
11:00 AM Build
12:00 PM Lunch
1:00 PM Build
4:00 PM Hard submission deadline
4:00 – 5:00 PM Demos (3 min limit)
5:00 – 5:30 PM 🏆 Audience voting and award ceremony
Judges
Charis Liang, Product Manager & UX Lead at Epic

Focus Tracks
🎙️ Track 1 · Voice & Audio Tutors
Tutors that listen as well as talk. Hear a student read or think out loud, catch exactly where they get stuck, and respond like a patient coach.
Ideas: a read-aloud fluency coach that hears which words a kid stumbles on · a think-aloud math tutor that spots the misconception in a spoken explanation · a speaking partner for language learners · voice-first learning for students with dyslexia or low vision
✍️ Track 2 · Vision, Handwriting & Documents
Learning happens on paper. Build AI that reads handwritten work, worksheets, diagrams, and textbook pages, and gives feedback on the steps, not just the final answer.
Ideas: snap a photo of handwritten math and get step-by-step feedback · grade a stack of scanned worksheets and group the common mistakes · turn a picture-book or textbook page into an interactive lesson · understand a student's science diagram or lab sketch
🎥 Track 3 · Video & Classroom Understanding
Video holds a lot of what happens in teaching and learning. Turn lectures, demonstrations, and classroom moments into feedback for students and teachers.
Ideas: turn a lecture video into chapters, a study guide, and a quiz · give teachers feedback on talk time and questioning from a classroom recording · watch a student's experiment or presentation and coach them on it · a video explainer that adapts to what the learner already knows
📡 Track 4 · Real-Time Multi-Modal Tutors & Agents
Tutors that work live, like sitting next to a great teacher. Combine live video, voice, and screen or camera input so the AI sees what the student is doing and helps in the moment.
Ideas: a tutor on a live video call that watches a student work a problem and nudges at the right time · a screen-aware coding or homework coach · a phone-camera lab assistant for hands-on science · an AR or camera guide that teaches by pointing at real objects
📖 Track 5 · Multi-Modal Storytelling
Stories are how kids learn to read, imagine, and remember. Build AI that blends voice, images, and video into stories that teach, react to the reader, and let kids create their own.
Ideas: turn a child's drawing and voice recording into an illustrated, narrated story · an interactive read-along that reacts to how the reader is doing · turn a history or science lesson into a narrated illustrated or video story · kids co-creating a story by voice, with images generated as they talk · multilingual narration that reads the same story in a child's home language
📊 Track 6 · Multi-Modal Learning Assessment
Build quick, fair, automated ways to understand where a learner is, using voice, handwriting, and interaction instead of long one-on-one tests.
Ideas: a reading-fluency screener that listens to a child read aloud · early dyslexia signals from speech and spelling · a math-fluency check from handwritten work · teacher-ready reports that turn results into next steps
🃏 Wildcard (Open Category)
Any multi-modal idea that doesn't fit the tracks above. If it solves a real problem in learning and shows a measurable learning outcome, build it.

About Event

On-Device AI Hackathon: Cleared for Takeoff ✈️
What if you could build an AI application that works, even when the Wi-Fi doesn't?
Your flight is preparing for takeoff. Once the cabin doors close, your connection to the cloud disappears. Before switching to airplane mode, you have one mission: build an AI project that runs entirely on-device.
In this hands-on hackathon from Qualcomm × Liquid AI , you'll team up with a flight crew of up to four people to build with Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) and Qualcomm iQ9s. At the end of the night, we'll turn off the Wi-Fi and put every project to the test.
Will your project survive offline?
Why on-device AI?
Unlike traditional AI applications that depend on cloud servers, on-device AI runs models directly on the user's hardware. That means your product can benefit from:
Low latency ⚡

Greater user privacy 🔒

No server inference costs 💸

Offline functionality 📴

Who this is for
👨‍💻 Developers who want to ship AI features without an inference bill

🤖 ML and AI engineers curious about deploying models beyond the cloud

⚙️ Edge, embedded, and robotics engineers building against real hardware constraints

🚀 Founders and product managers evaluating on-device versus cloud AI

🎓 Students and self-taught builders who want to leave having built something real

You don't need previous on-device development experience. If you can run a script, you can join the flight.
Teams may have up to four people . You can arrive with a team or meet your crew at the event.

ODSC × Nebius Hackathon: Build a Research Agent
📅 October 28–November 20, 2026
🌎 Kickoff at ODSC AI West + livestream | Virtual build
🎟️ Free and open to everyone
Check the main website →
Build an AI research agent that can search the web, bring evidence together, and give answers people can verify.
Join ODSC AI and Nebius for a hackathon focused on turning a research question into a useful, sourced answer. Start with the kickoff on October 28, then build at your own pace through November 20, with live online support from Nebius engineers along the way.
Your challenge: create a working research agent using Nebius Token Factory for open-model inference and Tavily for real-time web search. Your agent should connect its answers to credible sources, help users check key claims, and acknowledge when the evidence is incomplete.
Come solo, bring your team, or find teammates at the kickoff or online. AI and ML engineers, data scientists, developers, agent builders, and startup teams are all welcome.
Here’s how it works:
October 28 - Kickoff: Meet the Nebius team, get set up on Token Factory, and connect with other participants. Attend at ODSC AI West or join the livestream.

October 28–November 20 - Build: Develop your agent remotely, with online support available throughout the hackathon.

November 20 - Submission deadline: Submit a public repository with a README and a short demo. Registered participants will receive the submission link by email.

Projects will be evaluated on the quality of their evidence, whether the agent works from question to answer, its usefulness, its design, and its use of both required tools.
Registered participants also receive a complimentary ODSC AI West Expo pass . Winning projects will be promoted across ODSC channels, with a blog feature and an interview spotlight. Prizes and judges will be announced soon.
Registration is free, with no acceptance review. Join us and put your research agent to the test.

📅 October 28–November 20, 2026
🌎 Kickoff at ODSC AI West + livestream | Virtual build
🎟️ Free and open to everyone
Check the main website →
Build an AI research agent that can search the web, bring evidence together, and give answers people can verify.
Join ODSC AI and Nebius for a hackathon focused on turning a research question into a useful, sourced answer. Start with the kickoff on October 28, then build at your own pace through November 20, with live online support from Nebius engineers along the way.
Your challenge: create a working research agent using Nebius Token Factory for open-model inference and Tavily for real-time web search. Your agent should connect its answers to credible sources, help users check key claims, and acknowledge when the evidence is incomplete.
Come solo, bring your team, or find teammates at the kickoff or online. AI and ML engineers, data scientists, developers, agent builders, and startup teams are all welcome.
Here’s how it works:
October 28 - Kickoff: Meet the Nebius team, get set up on Token Factory, and connect with other participants. Attend at ODSC AI West or join the livestream.
October 28–November 20 - Build: Develop your agent remotely, with online support available throughout the hackathon.
November 20 - Submission deadline: Submit a public repository with a README and a short demo. Registered participants will receive the submission link by email.
Projects will be evaluated on the quality of their evidence, whether the agent works from question to answer, its usefulness, its design, and its use of both required tools.
Registered participants also receive a complimentary ODSC AI West Expo pass. Winning projects will be promoted across ODSC channels, with a blog feature and an interview spotlight. Prizes and judges will be announced soon.
Registration is free, with no acceptance review. Join us and put your research agent to the test.

Channel: Slack, Discord or Telegram

Build it. Code it. Put it to the test.
Forget everything you know about a traditional hackathon. This is one day, two tracks, and a whole lot of hardware.
Pick your challenge, build something real, and spend the day working alongside Qualcomm engineers and mentors who will help you take your project from idea to working demo.
Choose Your Track
⚽ Track 1: Train a Robot to Score
Your challenge: take a Qualcomm-powered robocar and teach it to see, navigate, find the goal, and score autonomously .
Using our Robot Soccer Cup resources, you'll work with robotics, computer vision, and on-device AI to train your robocar to complete the challenge entirely on its own.
There are no 1:1 matches this time. Instead, every team gets the same mission:
Which robocar can identify the goal and score first?
You'll have the day to build, tune, test, break things, fix them, and make your robot faster and smarter before putting it through the final challenge.
🕹️ Track 2: Build Your Own Arcade Game
Prefer building something you can play?
Grab an Arduino UNO Q Arcade Bundle and build your own arcade game from scratch.
You'll work with the UNO Q hardware and turn your idea into a playable experience by the end of the day. Make it nostalgic, competitive, weird, chaotic — that's entirely up to you.
What's in it for you?
🛠️ Real hands-on build time with hardware, AI, robotics, or game development — not slides, not theory

🤖 Two completely different tracks depending on what you want to explore

🤝 A full day with Qualcomm mentors and engineers on-site to help you troubleshoot, experiment, and keep building

📄 A project you can actually talk about on your resume, portfolio, or in interviews

🎒 No prior robotics or hardware experience required — we'll give you the resources you need to get started

🧰 All hardware provided by Qualcomm for both tracks

Before the Event
We don't want your first hour at the event to be spent figuring out where to start.
Qualcomm will provide Developer Journey Guides for both tracks so you can familiarize yourself with the hardware, tools, and challenge ahead of time.
We'll also host office hours before the event , giving you a chance to meet the mentors, ask questions, get your development environment ready, and make sure you're set up for success before the big day.
On event day, Qualcomm mentors will be available on-site throughout the entire experience to answer questions, help debug problems, and keep your project moving.
Step 1: Register on Luma today (Space is limited!)
Step 2: Check your Northeastern Email for a pre-event resources and updates
Step 3: Honor your spot + commitment by showing up and participating (or let us know if you can't make it so we can prepare accordingly)
Step 4: Remember to update your career capital (resume, LinkedIn, portfolios) with what you learned and built from this workshop!

This hack, we're headed back to Studio 45 for a hardware focused hack and build weekend in partnership with Claude Community and other partners.

There will also be chances to iterate on other parts of the workcell.
Track B: Opentrons
Build and test new liquid-handling workflows on the Flex.
Track C: Open build
We'll have extra robotic arms, cameras, and 3d printers for you to build on dexterity challenges or your own problem space.
You can also bring your own hardware.

Opentrons Robotics, a business unit of Opentrons Labworks, Inc., is the industry leader in flexible, user-friendly automation for life science labs. Our open-source ecosystem offers the scientific community the tools they need to automate experiments, share protocols and reproduce each other's results.

Pantograph is a research lab developing generally intelligent robots with simple, scalable methods. They are a public benefit corporation based in San Francisco.

SF Hardware Meetup , community of 10,000+ hardware professionals meeting monthly to building meaningful connections

About Event

Agenda
6:00 PM: Doors open

After that: Free conversation and networking

"The way to get startup ideas is not to try to think of startup ideas. It's to look for problems, preferably problems you have yourself." Paul Graham

Most people who want to build something sit in a room and brainstorm ideas. That is the wrong starting point.

The right starting point is a real problem. That is the ITCH worth scratching.

If you do not have that problem yourself, come find it here. ITCH is a panel discussion with business owners or industry experts in the SF community. We dig into what is actually hard in their business right now. Together, we find the ITCH.

You leave with a list of real problems you can actually work on. And some of the panelists might let you pilot your solution with them directly.You can find ways to leverage AI for these problems.

Industry
We're inviting a San Francisco retail owner who runs a physical clothing store and also designs and manufactures their own clothing line.

ITCHATHON
Two days later we run the ITCHATHON, a hackathon where we solve the problems we found here. Sign up for that too →

This is for anyone who wants to build something. A startup, a side project, or just something for your CV. Up to you.

Own Your AI: Build an Agentic AI Model Factory - Hack Night SF

Building AI Together | Union.ai

Register to See Address
San Francisco, CA

Registration

Welcome! To join the event, please register below.
Register

About Event

Build a Sovereign AI Model Factory: an ML Engineer Agent that evaluates, fine-tunes, deploys, and improves open models using Union on your cloud.
The best AI teams aren't renting every capability from an external API, they're building systems they own and control. In this hands-on session at the AWS Loft, we'll build exactly that.
We'll start with a walkthrough where we build a LangGraph-powered agent that evaluates open models in parallel, fine-tunes promising candidates, deploys the winner, and retrains automatically when performance drops. Think of it as the first brick in your own model factory : a repeatable system for evaluating, improving, and deploying models you control, not a black box you call and hope for the best.
Along the way, you'll see how Union.ai gives your workflows a durable runtime with infrastructure as context, so agents adapt infra resources, recover from failures, and keep moving without re-running completed work. And because it all runs in your own AWS account , you own the full stack end to end: your models, your data, your infrastructure, your IP.
Then we switch into hack night mode : keep building on the example, bring your own models or datasets, experiment with evals and fine-tuning, extend open models to different parts of your agent, or start something new around the same ideas.
For teams thinking about sovereign AI , this is a practical starting point for owning more of your stack, the weights, the training loop, the evals, and the infrastructure it runs on, all on AWS.
Bring a laptop. Leave with a factory.

All guests must be 18+ and present a valid government-issued physical photo ID at check-in (digital IDs are not accepted). Scooters and bikes are not permitted in any Amazon building, and there is no on-site parking.

About Event

NOTE: Early-bird sign-up via Luma is now over. Please visit https://startupweekendsandiego.com for additional details and registration.
******
UC San Diego's Design and Innovation Building hosts Techstars Startup Weekend San Diego, bringing builders, designers, lawyers, and the legally curious together for a weekend focused squarely on legal tech, software, and innovation. The theme: reimagining law for the AI era. The legal industry touches nearly everyone and has changed less than almost any other sector in the last few decades. This weekend is about building the tools that could finally change that, from AI that helps a tenant fight an eviction to software that lets a small business draft a contract without a $400-an-hour phone call.
Around 100 participants will pitch ideas, form teams around the strongest ones, and spend the weekend building toward a final pitch to a panel of judges. Mentors and coaches work alongside teams throughout, helping them get out of the building to validate ideas with real users, sharpen product direction, and prepare a polished final pitch.
Julian Bryant , Lead Organizer of Techstars Startup Weekend San Diego and an attorney/software developer himself, has facilitated roughly 40 Startup Weekends and brings a track record of real companies launched from the format, including CreativeUp, a Santa Barbara-based company that formed at one of his earliest events and is still operating more than six years later.
Jacques Chirazi , Director of the Basement and Entrepreneurship Center at UC San Diego's Office of Innovation and Commercialization, brings UC San Diego's student entrepreneurship ecosystem into the weekend, connecting participants to campus resources that can carry momentum well past Sunday night.
Mason Baldwin : TBD
This isn't just a competition, it's an entrepreneurial laboratory. Participants who've never attempted a startup get to try on different roles such as founder, designer, or engineer, and learn by doing what Julian calls "experiential education entrepreneurship," packed into three days.

About Event

Who Killed the Build? 💀
A Halloween DevTools Murder Mystery with Flox
The build is dead. The cause? Unknown.
Join AI Valley and Flox for a Halloween devtools night where you’ll investigate what went wrong, follow the clues, and figure out who (or what) killed the build.
Instead of a traditional product demo, Flox will take us through an interactive investigation of a broken development environment. Along the way, you’ll uncover suspicious dependencies, environment issues, and other clues before making your final guess.
🔎 Investigate the crime scene
💻 See Flox in action
🕵️ Follow the clues and solve the mystery
🎃 Enjoy Halloween food, drinks, and networking
Costumes are encouraged. Production incidents are not.

Hanwha AI Center (HAC) is a private membership for all those dedicated to AI. As a hub for innovation, HAC brings together passionate entrepreneurs, researchers, and visionaries to explore the societal and technological impacts of AI on human life.
Flox is a developer tool that creates reproducible, hash-pinned software environments across laptops, CI pipelines, and production. It eliminates environment drift by using a single configuration file to lock exact software versions everywhere. Flox is powered by the Nix package manager, but simplifies the experience so users do not have to write Nix code directly.

About Event

Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!
